x: In an exceptionally exciting and tough three miles cross-country race Jackie Hampshire won in grand style from two Guildford athletes who were at that time unbeaten this season; thus gaining revenge for a defeat these two recently inflicted upon him.
JACKIE HAMPSHIRE Sth. London X-country and 1 mile champion, will represent London in the Inter-area schools X-country Championships at Liverpool im March.

Bespectacled miler Jackie Hampshire achieved an outstanding performance in the Intermediate mile final of the All-England Schools Championships by finishing sixth in a new Club Youths record of 4:30.4.

Mitcham's 4:17 miler Malcolm Burton had moved his club into 2nd place after a sprint finish with Halliday (Hercules) and Jackie Hampshire, after fighting hard all thr way with Burton, lost a little ground on the run-in but had moved Belgrave into fourth place.

Gerards and Mitcham AC; but showing great form he fought off all his rivals to win a very close finish (only 4 secs separated the first 4 home) in a record time no less than 20secs inside the previous mark, held by our own Jackie Hampshire.
The first lap ended with Jackie Hampshire and T. Naish (Sutton) in the lead together, with Cocks, Fairclough and Morrison, packing well, close behind; giving Belgrave 5 in 6 at the half way stage.
Jackie Hampshire retained his hold on the 3 miles championship for Youths, winning from Tony Fairclough in a time only one second slower than last year's.
But the course was very much unsuited to the track style of our leading runners, save Jackie Hampshire, involving three laps of stiff hill-climbing.
Jackie Hampshire thoroughly enjoyed himself and passed 10 of those ahead to bring us up to 4th - an excellent performance which gave him one of the fastest times of the day.
Jackie Hampshire took over for the 3rd leg and held 3rd position; not an outstanding run but he appeared to be feeling the effect of the previous week's outing.
All in all, this was a most keenly contested race and congratulations are due to Jackie Hampshire becoming the first youth to complete a hat-trick of wins in this championship.
Of our lads, David Cocks was first home in 13th position, Ken Redwood 22nd, Jackie Hampshire, suffering from vaccination effects, 41st and the team was completed by Peter Edwards in 96th position.
It soon became evident that we were possible winners for Tony Fairclough was with the leaders followed closely by Chris Steer with David Cocks and Jackie Hampshire not far behind.

Dave Cocks started slowly, probably because he had been short of training, but he soon worked his way through to become our second scorer, a little ahead of Keith Angus who flogged his way round the two circuits with great spirit. Jackie Hampshire rose to the occasion once more and closed-in the team with a fine 118th.

Jackie Hampshire, with an inspired run, picked off these teams in steady succession and he did hand over to Charlie Dabbs in 6th place. Unfortunately, Chas had a 46 sec. gap to close on the 5th team (Mitcham) and a further 14 secs. and 33 secs. respectively on Herne Hill and Guildford.

Jackie Hampshire on the second leg kept in close contact with the teams in front, and Chris Steer moved up five places to sixth on the third leg but, by this time, the leaders were well ahead and, with no stars to call on, the possibility of a 'place' looked somewhat unlikely.

With John Moore then 20th, Dave Cocks 49th and Jackie Hampshire moving through in the 70's, there was still an outside chance of a team place, but Chris then had a bad bout of "stitch" which sent him back 40 places in the space of a mile, and with our other runners roughly holding their positions we…
Jackie Hampshire ran well enough to have scored in all but the first three teams, yet was Belgrave's 12th man home in 83rd place. Needless to say, we took the "twelve" cup!

Jackie Hampshire ran particularly well to be our 2nd scoring man in 12th place; how this lad always rises to the big occasion! At the end of the sixth leg our lead which at one time was over 1½ minutes, was whittled down and it was not surprising that Jackie Hampshire on the 7th leg had to give way to Derek Fernee of Poly.

Jackie Hampshire ran well on the fourth leg and held our position, putting us within striking distance of SLH, TVH and Hercules, 'B' teams. Chris Steer soon disposed of these and left it to Tony Fairclough to pass HHH and Ponders End, bringing us home 8th.

Charlie Walker had not had a good winter season, and although he gave of his utmost on stage 4 it was nowhere near his old best, and he handed over to Jackie Hampshire a full minute behind 3rd place and 2 mins 11secs behind the new leaders--Cambridge H.
The ever-reliable Jackie Hampshire was our next man (148) followed by Dave Cocks and Alan Morrison, both below their best. A disappointing points total of 673 gave us a lowly 28th team placing.
Two runners who improved by minutes on their previous week's run over the same course were Howard Satchell and Jackie Hampshire. Team result. scoring 20 a side: TVH 280 pts BELGRAVE H 541 pts
Congratulations to Jackie Hampshire who was married on 29th April. It only seems a couple of years ago that he was our fastest boy miler.
